name: Mexico
description: Mexico from the Olmecs, Teotihuacan, the Maya and the Aztecs to the Spanish conquest, independence, revolution and the modern country.

checkpoints.name: Ancient Mexico
checkpoints.note: The Olmecs carved giant heads on the Gulf coast. Teotihuacan became one of the largest cities in the world, the Maya built cities in the south, and the Aztecs ruled from Tenochtitlan on its lake.

checkpoints.name: New Spain
checkpoints.note: Cortés took Tenochtitlan in 1521 and Mexico City rose on its ruins. For three centuries New Spain sent silver to Europe, and a new culture mixed the Indigenous and the Spanish.

checkpoints.name: Independence and revolution
checkpoints.note: Hidalgo's cry of 1810 began the fight for independence, won in 1821. Mexico lost half its land to the United States, Juárez beat the French, Díaz ruled long, and the revolution of 1910 shook the country for a decade.

checkpoints.name: Modern Mexico
checkpoints.note: One party ruled for seventy years while the muralists and Kahlo painted and Mexico City grew vast. Trade with the north opened in 1994, democracy deepened in 2000, and in 2024 the first woman president was elected.
